title: O Thou Eternal One in Three
description: O Thou Eternal One in Three in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Latin hymns of the early Church for Hymns of the Early Church (London, 1896), headed “Tu Trinitatis Unitas”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Thou E-ter-nal One in Three, Dread Ru-ler of the earth and sky, Ac-cept the praise we yield to Thee, Who, wa-king, lift our songs on high.

lines: O Thou Eternal One in Three,
Dread Ruler of the earth and sky,
Accept the praise we yield to Thee,
Who, waking, lift our songs on high.
Now from the couch of rest we rise,
While solemn night in silence reigns,
And lift to Thee our earnest cries,
To give Thy balm to heal our pains.
If in the night by Satan’s guile
Our souls were lured by thought of sin;
O bid Thy light celestial smile,
And chase away the night within.
Purge Thou our flesh from every stain,
Let not dull sloth our hearts depress;
Nor let the sense of guilt remain,
To chill the warmth our souls possess.
To Thee, Redeemer blest, we pray,
That in our souls Thy light may shine;
So we shall walk from day to day,
Unerring in Thy way Divine.
Grant it, O Father, in Thy love,
Grant it, O One-begotten Son,
Who with the Spirit reign above,
Now, and while endless ages run.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Early Church (1896)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Latin, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Early Church; set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
